summary: Goat Ridge L-4 cab with basement, built 1933-34 in the Gifford Pinchot forest, was in use in 1963, probably removed in 1966, and is now a dead-end site on a Goat Rocks hike.

facts.status_note: Cab gone by the 1960s; WillhiteWeb says probably removed in 1966. One WillhiteWeb photo is captioned Old lookout parts.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Gifford Pinchot National Forest)

access.note: Trail loop from the Berry Patch trailhead; the route climbs into the Goat Rocks Wilderness.

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb lists the loop as 2 miles, reached by Forest Road 21 and then Forest Road 2150 to the trailhead. The lookout site is a dead end off the loop.

events.note: L-4 cab with basement built in 1933 by Oscar Boyer and other CCC crews; finishing work in 1934
Two Packwood district lookouts manned in late June 1963, Goat Ridge among them; WillhiteWeb says still in use by the Forest Service that year
WillhiteWeb says probably removed in 1966; firetower.org says gone by the 1960s
Hike report calls the spot the former lookout site

notes_for_editor: Built 1933 (firetower, firelookout, WillhiteWeb) agrees. Removal: firetower and firelookout say gone by the 1960s; WillhiteWeb says probably 1966 after use in 1963; treated as consistent. Elevation: brief 1902 m matches firelookout 6240 ft; WillhiteWeb gives lookout site 6,201 ft and ridge highpoint 6240+. Brief access 'unknown' is answered by WillhiteWeb (public trail, no permit mentioned). The 1963 staffing rests on a newspaper item quoted by washingtonlookouts.weebly.com; the 1963 use is also in WillhiteWeb. Search snippets for Mountaineers and trailchick mention scattered artifacts at the site, but those pages did not yield fetchable text, so not used. No source describes remains beyond the Old lookout parts caption; a site-condition check would firm up today's section. Story says the site is a dead end off the loop, which WillhiteWeb states.
